versions.research_rationale: EO 9591 of July 21, 1945 (official text 10 FR 9205, saved OCR text layer of the govinfo issue PDF read in full). The OCR interleaves columns: the order's heading, enacting clause and paragraphs 1-2 run continuously, then text of EO 9592 and a Civil Service Commission rule intervene before the signature block 'July 21,1945' with F.R. Doc. 45-13508 (EO 9592 carries 45-13509 and its own signature), so the order consists of paragraphs 1 and 2 only. Paragraph 1's opening words are quoted up to the parenthetical citation because the OCR fuses footnote markers to the cited order numbers there (the fused figures are not valid order numbers); the parenthetical cites EO 7968 as amended by EOs 8297, 9303, 9407 and 9507. Paragraph 1 amends Tariff Items 6, 8 and 34; paragraph 2 amends section V-23 of the Foreign Service Regulations. EO 9767 (1946) and EO 10473 (1953) changed other sub-items of Item 6 but not the eighth heading 'Issue of card or certificate of identity and registration' (EO 10473 inserts a new item immediately below it, so it still stood in 1953), Item 8 or Item 34; EO 10639 (1955) deleted only Items 1-5. EO 10697 (22 FR 777, read in full) prescribed a complete new Tariff effective March 1, 1957 and in section 7 revoked EO 9591, so paragraph 1's clauses first ended 1957-03-01. Paragraph 2 is left open (see the gap): its host section V-23 may have lapsed earlier. This is a partial claim: original text, clause inventory, savings and later-source search are asserted; the ending is not.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 10697 contains no savings or transition clause. It prescribes a complete new Tariff of Fees and its own collection rules (sections 1-6), effective March 1, 1957, and revokes the earlier tariff orders to the extent not already revoked or superseded. Fees charged under the earlier tariff were completed transactions; the order created no fund, office, property or vested right that survived. Paragraph 2's wording change and revocation in section V-23 of the Foreign Service Regulations created no fund, office, property or vested right either.

unresolved_material_gaps: First end of paragraph 2 (amendments of section V-23 of the Foreign Service Regulations, EO 7968) not established: EO 10697 section 7 revokes EO 9591 and EO 7968 only 'To the extent that they have not heretofore been revoked or superseded', and section V-23 (22 CFR 105.23 in 1945) may have been superseded earlier by the Foreign Service Act of 1946 or by later departmental finance regulations; no held source shows whether V-23 was still in force on March 1, 1957, so first_end and whole_order_end are left open.
claim.research_rationale: EO 9591 of July 21, 1945 (official text 10 FR 9205, saved OCR text layer of the govinfo issue PDF read in full). The OCR interleaves columns: the order's heading, enacting clause and paragraphs 1-2 run continuously, then text of EO 9592 and a Civil Service Commission rule intervene before the signature block 'July 21,1945' with F.R. Doc. 45-13508 (EO 9592 carries 45-13509 and its own signature), so the order consists of paragraphs 1 and 2 only. Paragraph 1's opening words are quoted up to the parenthetical citation because the OCR fuses footnote markers to the cited order numbers there (the fused figures are not valid order numbers); the parenthetical cites EO 7968 as amended by EOs 8297, 9303, 9407 and 9507. Paragraph 1 amends Tariff Items 6, 8 and 34; paragraph 2 amends section V-23 of the Foreign Service Regulations. EO 9767 (1946) and EO 10473 (1953) changed other sub-items of Item 6 but not the eighth heading 'Issue of card or certificate of identity and registration' (EO 10473 inserts a new item immediately below it, so it still stood in 1953), Item 8 or Item 34; EO 10639 (1955) deleted only Items 1-5. EO 10697 (22 FR 777, read in full) prescribed a complete new Tariff effective March 1, 1957 and in section 7 revoked EO 9591, so paragraph 1's clauses first ended 1957-03-01. Paragraph 2 is left open (see the gap): its host section V-23 may have lapsed earlier. This is a partial claim: original text, clause inventory, savings and later-source search are asserted; the ending is not.
